questions.q: What problem does Adaptive Query Execution (AQE) solve?
options: Spark's upfront query plan is based on estimated statistics that can be stale or wrong — AQE re-optimizes using real, measured stats at runtime
It replaces the need for a cluster to run any Spark job
It permanently caches every table a query touches
It converts Python UDFs into native C++ code
questions.explain: AQE corrects the plan using real numbers measured from completed stages, not just the planner's upfront guess.

questions.q: What does dynamic partition coalescing fix?
options: A shuffle producing too many tiny, mostly-empty partitions after a filter removes most of the data
A query that reads from the wrong table entirely
A cluster that has too few worker nodes
A join that uses too much broadcast memory
questions.explain: AQE measures actual post-shuffle partition sizes and merges tiny ones into fewer, right-sized partitions.

questions.q: When can AQE switch a sort-merge join to a broadcast join?
options: After the shuffle, once the actual size of one side of the join turns out small enough to broadcast
Before the query even starts running
Only when Photon is disabled on the cluster
Never — join strategy is always fixed upfront
questions.explain: The upfront planner can't safely choose a broadcast join without knowing the real size of the data; AQE can switch once that size is measured.

questions.q: Why doesn't adding more cluster nodes fix a skewed shuffle partition?
options: One oversized partition still runs as a single task that can't be split across nodes on its own — more nodes just sit idle
More nodes always make every query slower
Skew only happens on clusters with too much memory
Cluster size has no relationship to shuffle performance at all
questions.explain: A single task processing one skewed partition is the bottleneck — AQE's skew handling splits that partition, which adding hardware alone cannot do.

questions.q: How does AQE's skew join handling address a disproportionately large partition?
options: It splits the oversized partition into smaller sub-partitions that can be processed in parallel across multiple tasks
It deletes the rows causing the skew
It moves the entire query to a different cluster
It disables shuffling for the rest of the query
questions.explain: Splitting the oversized partition turns one long straggler task into several parallel tasks, closer in size to the rest.
